title: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitors and the Risk of Congenital Malformations
authors: Bateman BT, Patorno E, Desai RJ, Seely EW, Mogun H, Dejene SZ, et al.
population: Completed pregnancies linked to liveborn infants in US Medicaid claims, 2000 to 2010; 4107 (0.31%) exposed to ACE inhibitors in the first trimester

authorConflicts: The Pharmacoepidemiology Program at the Harvard School of Public Health is supported by Pfizer, Takeda, Bayer and Asisa; Huybrechts, Bateman and Hernandez-Diaz are investigators on grants to Brigham and Women's Hospital from Lilly and Pfizer, and Bateman from Baxalta, all stated as unrelated; Hernandez-Diaz has consulted for Boehringer-Ingelheim and UCB, and Bateman for Optum.
result: Unadjusted, malformations occurred in 5.9% of ACE-inhibitor-exposed against 3.3% of unexposed pregnancies (relative risk 1.82, 95% CI 1.61 to 2.06) and cardiac malformations in 3.4% against 1.2% (2.95, 2.50 to 3.47). Restricted to pregnancies with chronic hypertension and adjusted for confounders, relative risks were 0.89 (0.75 to 1.06) for any malformation, 0.95 (0.75 to 1.21) for cardiac and 0.54 (0.26 to 1.11) for central nervous system malformations.
